# Your first count in 30 minutes {#sec-first-count}

#| include: false
source(here::here("_common.R"))

::: {.audience}
For the owner, starting out
:::

::: {.learn}
- How to get from a new install to a finished count, one step at a time.
- What the app asks for along the way, and what it can wait for.
- Where to read more when you want it.
:::

## The idea

You don't need to read this whole guide before you start. Five products and
one tray are enough to see how Jholok works. This chapter takes you from
opening the app for the first time to a finished count, in about half an hour.
Everything else can come later, when you need it.

If you count on your own, you don't need to set up any staff first. Jholok
lets the owner count, check and finish a count alone, and says so on the
result.

## In the app

### 1. Open Jholok

Open the app. A new install opens straight in: there's nothing to protect yet,
so it doesn't ask for your passcode. The Overview welcomes you and shows the
first of three steps.

```{r}
screenshot("overview-first-run.png")
```

The card shows one step at a time. Its last line says what comes next, and
the × hides it if you'd rather find your own way.

### 2. Add your products

Tap **Add product**. Give it a name, such as "Jhumka", and choose its type,
such as Earrings. Everything else is optional: Jholok makes up a product code
(the [SKU](glossary.qmd#sku)) if you leave it blank, and you can add the cost,
price and a photo later. Add four or five products this way.

If your products are already in a spreadsheet, tap **Import catalogue**
instead and choose the file. It needs a column for the name and one for the
type, saved as CSV. @sec-catalogue explains the other columns.

### 3. Count one tray

When you have products, the card moves on to **Count one tray**. Tap
**Start a count**.

- **Location**: where you're counting, such as "Front tray".
- **What to count**: leave **All types** on, or choose just the type in the
  tray.

Tap **Start**. Now count what's in front of you: tap **+** once for each
piece, or tap the number to type it. If there are none of a product, tap the
**0** on its row for None here. Nothing on this screen shows how many
there should be. That is on purpose: a count that can't see the answer can't
be swayed by it. @sec-counting explains why.

```{r}
screenshot("counting-solo.png")
```

If the tray is a box of pieces on cards, tap **Box photo** to count it from a
photo instead. @sec-boxes covers that; for a first count, counting by hand is
fine.

### 4. Review the count

When you've counted, tap **Review** at the top. Jholok asks for your Face ID
or passcode once, then shows what you found next to what the records say:
which products matched, which are short and which are over.

A product you counted short is marked **Recount first**: count it once more
before it can change anything. @sec-review explains each part of Review.

### 5. Complete it

Tap **Complete count**. The sheet says what completing will change. A reason
is optional; without one the count says "Stock count".

```{r}
screenshot("complete-solo.png")
```

Tap **Complete count** again. The stock of the products you ticked is set to
what you counted, and the count is saved for good, with who did it: "The owner
(People not set up)".

That's your first count.

### What happens next

- **The lock starts.** Now that Jholok holds your stock, it asks for your Face
  ID or passcode when it opens. The first time, it explains why.
- **The card's last step** asks about the people who count. Tap **I count
  alone** if that's you, or **Set up People** to add staff, each with a PIN
  (@sec-setting-up).
- **Make a backup.** Your stock lives only on this phone. Settings → Backup
  saves a copy elsewhere (@sec-keeping-data-safe).

::: {.remember}
- Five products and one tray are enough to start.
- Counting is blind: the count never shows what there should be.
- Alone, you count, review and complete yourself; the result says so.
- Back up once your real stock is in.
:::
